# crafty_schedule

Manage recurring commands using a token with server SCHEDULE permission.

```terraform
resource "crafty_schedule" "announcement" {
  server_id     = crafty_minecraft_server.example.id
  name          = "Hourly announcement"
  command       = "say Remember to back up your world"
  interval      = 1
  interval_type = "hours"
  enabled       = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `command` (String) Command queued by Crafty, such as a console command or restart_server.
- `name` (String) Schedule display name.
- `server_id` (String) Crafty server ID.

### Optional

- `action` (String) Crafty action label. Defaults to command; command determines the queued operation.
- `cron_string` (String) Five-field APScheduler cron expression in Crafty's host timezone. Overrides interval settings.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the scheduler runs this task. Must be true when creating.
- `interval` (Number) Positive interval count. Ignored when cron_string is set.
- `interval_type` (String) minutes, hours, or days. Ignored when cron_string is set; defaults to hours.
- `start_time` (String) HH:MM in Crafty's host timezone, used for days schedules. Defaults to 00:00.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Crafty schedule ID.



## Scheduling and limitations

`cron_string` overrides interval settings. It uses five APScheduler fields in the
Crafty host's timezone; numeric weekdays run from Monday (`0`) through Sunday (`6`).
Prefer names such as `mon`. For `days`, Crafty selects every Nth day of the month
at `start_time`, rather than measuring elapsed 24-hour periods.

Creation requires `enabled = true`: Crafty persists disabled tasks without
returning their ID. Existing or imported tasks can be disabled. Refresh only reads
configuration. One-time tasks, task chains and backup policy references are not supported.

Read errors preserve state. Crafty returns HTTP 500 for a deleted task, which cannot
be distinguished from a server error. After independently confirming permanent
deletion, back up state and use `terraform state rm` before recreating the task.

## Import

```sh
terraform import crafty_schedule.announcement SERVER_ID/SCHEDULE_ID
```
